title: Which product fits whom, and four questions before moving up
objectives: Match five client needs to the best-fit product and the reason.
Ask the four ladder questions before moving a client up.
body_md:
Building wealth from salary, any amount: mutual funds (SIP) — low minimum, diversified, liquid, low cost. Emergency money or goals under 3 years: liquid / debt mutual funds — stability and quick access. Large surplus, wants own portfolio and transparency: PMS — personal portfolio, full visibility, some customisation. ₹1 crore+, long horizon, wants private-market exposure: Category I / II AIF — access to unlisted companies, private credit, real estate. ₹1 crore+, wants hedged or complex strategies: Category III AIF — long-short, hedge-style approaches.

| Client need | Best fit | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Building wealth from salary, any amount | Mutual funds (SIP) | Low minimum, diversified, liquid, low cost |
| Emergency money or goals under 3 years | Liquid / debt mutual funds | Stability and quick access |
| Large surplus, wants own portfolio and transparency | PMS | Personal portfolio, full visibility, some customisation |
| ₹1 crore+, long horizon, wants private-market exposure | Category I / II AIF | Access to unlisted companies, private credit, real estate |
| ₹1 crore+, wants hedged or complex strategies | Category III AIF | Long-short, hedge-style approaches |

Questions before moving a client up the ladder: “What share of your total investments would this be?” “Could you leave this money untouched for 5–7 years, with no option to exit early?” (critical for Cat I & II AIFs). “Is your mutual fund core already in place?” “Are you comfortable with less frequent valuations and less liquidity?”
example: ₹5 crore client wanting ₹2 crore in a PE AIF but needing ₹50 lakh in two years for a house: keep the house money liquid; size the AIF only from money not needed for years.
say: Ask: could you leave this untouched for 5–7 years?
Eligible is not the same as suitable.

check.q: A client meets the ₹1 crore AIF minimum. Does that make them suitable?
o: No — eligible is not suitable; check lock-in tolerance and the core portfolio
